fields.name: StopPeers
fields.evidence: Toolkit EoCServer.dll esv::TimelineSystem::ConfirmPeerStop fetches the 0x28-byte component (EoCServer.dll+0xE66400) of the timeline entity and removes the handshake's peer id (StopHandshake+0x10) from the array at +0 with EoCServer.dll+0x519290 (linear search over 4-byte elements, the assert names ls::SpanIterator<TypeWrap<int, net::PeerIDClassname>>). Windows: the component destructor bg3.exe+0x6A2280 (registered with the storage in bg3.exe+0x21C8C50, size 0x28) clears and frees plain Arrays at +0 and +0x10 and nothing else.

fields.name: DestructionPeers
fields.evidence: Toolkit esv::TimelineSystem::ConfirmPeerDestruction removes the peer id of the DestroyHandshake from the array at +0x10 of the same component with the same function. Windows destructor bg3.exe+0x6A2280 frees the array at +0x10.

fields.name: field_20
fields.evidence: Plain data: the Windows destructor bg3.exe+0x6A2280 does not touch +0x20. By analogy with esv::ServerTimelineCreationConfirmationComponent (Timeout float + flags after its containers) probably a timeout and flags; no writer found.

open_questions: Element width (4-byte net::PeerID) and the member roles come from the Toolkit (esv::TimelineSystem::ConfirmPeerStop / ConfirmPeerDestruction); bg3.exe has no counterpart of those functions (decomp.py matches --all finds none).
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Found the Windows component destructor bg3.exe+0x6A2280 through the storage registration bg3.exe+0x21C8C50: two plain Arrays at +0 and +0x10, plain data after - confirming the Toolkit offsets; element width and +0x20 stay Toolkit/unknown.
